items.title: Moody's cuts Botswana rating again as diamond slump weighs on economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ratings agency Moody's on Friday downgraded Botswana's domestic- and foreign-currency long-term issuer ratings to "Baa2" from "Baa1", citing an expected deterioration in the country's public finances. The move marks Botswana's second downgrade by Moody's in less than a year, leaving the sovereign just two notches above junk status. It also comes days after Finance Minister Ndaba Gaolathe said Botswana expects a much smaller budget deficit in the current fiscal year, helped by higher-than-expected revenue from the central bank and measures to rein in spending.

items.title: Trump says he does not want to 'integrate' with China on AI
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that despite a "big talk" this week with Chinese President Xi Jinping on AI, the US should not join efforts with China on the technology. "We had a big talk on SI," Trump told reporters at the White House, using his preferred name of super intelligence. Trump said he did not want to "integrate" AI initiatives with China because of US dominance.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan police say hostel tragedy linked to Form Four student ‘punishing’ junior for breaking rules
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Sept 27 — Police yesterday confirmed that preliminary investigations into the death of a Form Two student at a school in Kuala Pilah, Negeri Sembilan, suggest the incident stemmed from the victim’s alleged breach of school rules. Following this, the suspect — a Form Four student — is believed to have reprimanded and “punished” the younger boy over the offence. According to Astro Awani , Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said that the suspect has been remanded for six days beginning Saturday to assist investigations, after the application was filed at the Seremban Magistrates’ Court.

items.title: US to finalise sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Unites States Transportation Department on Monday will finalise sharply lower vehicle fuel economy standards through 2031, reversing a push by the Biden administration to force automakers to build more electric vehicles, officials said on Saturday. President Donald Trump said he had approved new fuel economy standards for cars and trucks, which he said will lower the price of new vehicles. The new standards would cut the cost of new vehicles but increase fuel consumption and carbon dioxide emissions for decades, according to the department's own estimates.

items.title: ‘Malaysia will speak plainly: We are sick of it’: Mohamad Hasan tells UN to act on Gaza
items.summary: NEW YORK, Sept 27 — The United Nations (UN) must move from reacting to crises to preventing them, with the task particularly urgent in Gaza, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. We must move from reaction to prevention,” he said in his national statement at the General Debate of the 81st UN General Assembly here on Saturday. Mohamad said nowhere was that task more urgent than in Gaza.

items.title: Thousands march in Madrid over eviction of 87-year-old woman
items.summary: MADRID: Thousands of people marched through Madrid on Saturday to protest the eviction earlier this week of an 87-year-old woman from her lifelong home, calling for greater protection for tenants. Images of Maricarmen Abascal being carried from her Madrid flat on a stretcher on Wednesday after police broke down her door have thrust Spain's housing crisis back into the spotlight ahead of a general election due in 2027. Protesters rattled keys, blew whistles, chanted slogans and held banners calling for measures to curb rising housing costs and make evictions more difficult as they marched through central Madrid.

items.title: Ringgit expected to trade range-bound next week ahead of key US data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade within a narrow range against the US dollar next week as investors await key United States economic data for further clues on the direction of interest rates. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said attention would be on the US labour market next week, particularly the nonfarm payrolls report which is due to be released on Oct 2. "We expect the ringgit to trade within a range of around RM4.07 to RM4.10 against the US dollar next week," he told Bernama.

items.title: Bargain hunting seen on Bursa Malaysia next week
items.summary: On the index board, the FBM Emas Index rose 44.92 points to 12,456.64, the FBM Top 100 Index gained 33.09 points to 12,243.46, the FBM Emas Shariah Index shed 5.76 points to 12,306.23 and the FBM ACE Index expanded 288.26 points to 5,532.86, while the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 0.89 of a point to 17,844.91. Weekly turnover firmed to 17.11 billion units worth RM14.07 billion from 15.02 billion units worth RM14.18 billion in the previous week. Main Market volume improved to 10.41 billion units valued at RM12.31 billion, from 9.38 billion units valued at RM12.93 billion previously.

items.title: Malaysia calls for UN to challenge, abolish Security Council veto
items.summary: NEW YORK, Sept 27 — The veto power of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) must be challenged and ultimately abolished to address the Council’s failures, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said. Mohamad said Resolution 76/262 had already created an accountability channel between the Security Council and the General Assembly. He said the international community must begin work now to reform the Security Council.

items.title: Kids under 14 make up more than a third of Kelantan’s drowning deaths since 2023
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 27 — Children under 14 accounted for about 36 per cent of the 96 drowning deaths recorded in Kelantan since 2023, highlighting the urgent need to strengthen preventive measures and water safety awareness for this group. Kelantan Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Farhan Sufyan Borhan said out of the total fatalities, 35 victims were children, with the highest figure of 14 deaths recorded in 2024. Consequently, Farhan Sufyan said Kelantan JBPM is increasing preventive efforts through water safety education and awareness, including the free Program Jom Renang (Let’s Swim Programme) conducted in five series involving 300 children under 12 at various locations statewide.

items.title: MM2H brings in RM8.85b in economic value in less than two years
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — The Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) programme generated RM8.85 billion in economic value between Oct 1, 2024 and Aug 31, 2026, including more than RM5 billion in property purchases and RM3.82 billion in fixed deposits. Deputy Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Chiew Choon Man said the programme received 7,650 new applications during the same period across the Platinum, Gold, Silver and Special Economic Zone categories. Chiew said China led the applications with 3,847, followed by Taiwan (1,054), Hong Kong (324), Singapore (287) and the United States (284).

items.title: UNSC veto power must be challenged, abolished - Tok Mat
items.summary: NEW YORK: Malaysia has stressed that the use of veto power at the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) must be questioned and firmly challenged, particularly in cases involving crimes against humanity. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said global confidence in the world body's ability to act was now at its lowest point. Mohamad said Resolution 76/262 had established an accountability channel between the UNSC and the General Assembly.

items.title: Anwar: Knowledge, not anger, must drive the nation forward
items.summary: BANGI, Sept 27 — A country will be crippled if driven by anger, but must instead be guided by knowledge, which forms the foundation for its strength, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said the strength of any struggle could not depend solely on spirit and emotion, but must instead be supported by the strength of knowledge capable of raising public awareness and instilling a sense of responsibility. Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan.

items.title: 4 men killed after car crashes into parked lorry in Sepanggar
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Four men were killed after the Perodua Viva car they were travelling in skidded and crashed into a five-tonne lorry parked on the road shoulder at Taman Jaya Diri, Jalan Sepanggar, early today. It said personnel from the Kota Kinabalu fire and rescue station, assisted by the Lintas fire and rescue station, arrived at the scene at 2.59am and found all four victims, whose identities are still being ascertained, trapped inside the vehicle. "Four victims were trapped inside the vehicle, and the firemen used special rescue equipment to extricate them," it said in a statement.

items.title: Teen worker’s hand trapped in meat grinder at Ipoh chicken factory
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 27 — An Orang Asli man suffered injuries after his right hand became trapped in a meat grinder during an incident at a chicken processing factory in Bercham Light Industrial Area here today. “The incident involved a 19-year-old worker whose right hand was trapped in a meat grinder. Upon arrival, the fire engine crew found that the victim’s hand was still inside the machine and the victim remained conscious.

items.title: ‘Hari Cuci Malaysia’ sets two new records with 272,390 people, 89 tonnes of recyclables
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 27 — Hari Cuci Malaysia (HCM) 2026 set two new records in the Malaysia Book of Records (MBOR) yesterday through large-scale public mobilisation and recyclable material collection in a single day. The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said in a statement that the two records were set with 272,390 people nationwide participating in HCM 2026 and the collection of 89,221.22 kilogrammes of recyclable materials in one day. In addition, HCM 2026, conducted simultaneously across 469 locations nationwide, collected 8,010.19 tonnes of solid waste through cleaning activities and gotong-royong initiatives.

items.title: Police to quiz former Negri Sembilan exco members
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bukit Aman is expected to record statements from the 10 Negri Sembilan executive councillors whose appointments were revoked. "An officer from Bukit Aman will travel to Negri Sembilan tomorrow (today). The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has revoked the appointments of members of the state executive council after they were found to have breached their oath of office .

items.title: Death toll from Indonesia ferry sinking jumps to 64
items.summary: JAKARTA: The death toll after a ferry sank in Indonesia's Java Sea almost two weeks ago has jumped to 64, an official said on Saturday, as rescuers extended the search for dozens still missing. Rescuers recovered four bodies from the submerged ship on Saturday, while seven others were found along the shoreline, Yudhi said. He added that the search operation would be extended a further seven days but will be evaluated every three days.

items.title: 5.2-magnitude quake hits Papua New Guinea
items.summary: BEIJING: A 5.2 magnitude earthquake jolted New Britain Region, Papua New Guinea, at 2149 GMT on Saturday, the GFZ German Research Centre for Geosciences said, according to Xinhua. The epicentre was located at a depth of 10km, at latitude 4.59 degrees south and longitude 152.87 degrees east. – BERNAMA-XINHUA © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Building resilient padi farming to strengthen Malaysia's food security
items.summary: STRENGTHENING the nation's food security involves not only producing more food, but also building a resilient domestic agricultural ecosystem that can sustain farmers and domestic supply over the long term. Through the Nestle Paddy Club (NPC), farmers cultivate more than 600ha of padi. "Rice is an important ingredient.

items.title: Pope prays at Lourdes after huge Paris mass
items.summary: LOURDES, France: Pope Leo XIV prayed for France on Saturday at its holy shrine in Lourdes, after riding along the Champs Elysees in the popemobile and holding an emotional open-air mass in front of hundreds of thousands of worshippers in Paris. The leader of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics is on a four-day trip to France, a secular country with deep Catholic roots, on the first official papal visit there in nearly two decades. GIANT PARIS MASS In an earlier highlight of the visit's second day, the 71-year-old pope led enthusiastic worshippers in a mass at Paris's Place de la Concorde, where a giant white canopy had been erected to serve as a makeshift altar.

items.title: Trump rejects Iran proposal for deal to reopen Hormuz
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Saturday rejected a truce deal proposed by Iran that Teheran said could have reopened the Strait of Hormuz to shipping within a week. "I reject their proposal," Trump told reporters outside the White House. On the seventh day of the truce, Iran would reopen Hormuz.

items.title: From trade fair to carnival, a look back at Pesta Pulau Pinang as its five-decade home makes way for LRT
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 27 — For the first time in over five decades, Pesta Pulau Pinang will not be held on the grounds Penangites have long called home. December 2025 marked the last time Pesta was held at Sungai Nibong. Pesta Pulau Pinang arch at Esplanade in 1966.

items.title: Country cannot tolerate corruption, plundering of national wealth, says Anwar
items.summary: BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government respects the Federal Constitution and the decision of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong regarding former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's case. He said this did not prevent him from offering views and advice based on jurisprudence, the law and the nation's interests. He said the government's position was clear that the country could not tolerate corruption or the act of taking national wealth for personal gain.

items.title: Proton Iswara steals the show in Apple's iPhone 18 Pro promo [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The appearance of a Proton Iswara in Apple's promotional video for the iPhone 18 Pro has caught the attention of social media users in Malaysia. The appearance of the car was quickly spotted by Malaysian social media users, with Apple's comment section filled with reactions such as "I saw Proton Saga there", "Wait, is that Malaysia Proton car?" View this post on Instagram A post shared by apple (@apple) Some users also joked about the appearance of the national car, leaving comments such as "Malaysia mendunia (goes global)" and "I saw Proton, I press LIKE."

items.title: Militant attack kills 11 at security check post in northern Pakistan
items.summary: PESHAWAR: Militants rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into a security check post in northern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people and wounding 18 others, police and rescue officials said Saturday. Saifullah Khan, a Dera Ismail Khan police official, told AFP that the attack on the security check post – which is jointly operated by police, military and customs personnel – took place "around noon." Earlier this month, at least 31 people, including 16 police personnel, were killed in an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters at Kohat, a town of around 220,000 people in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) province.

items.title: Teen's hand trapped in meat grinder at Ipoh premises
items.summary: IPOH: A 19-year-old Orang Asli teenager was injured after his right hand became trapped in a meat grinder at a premises in the Bercham 10 Light Industrial Area here today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received a distress call at 4.41pm. He said eight personnel from the Ipoh Fire and Rescue Station were dispatched to the location to rescue the teenager.

items.title: 'As many as it takes': Peepal Baba's half-century mission to reforest India
items.summary: WITH Delhi's choking haze hanging overhead, Peepal Baba presses a young tree into the earth, continuing a nearly half-century mission to restore India's vanishing green cover. "When I was young, I planted saplings like a soldier," said Swami Prem Parivartan, better known as "Peepal Baba", or "tree father", rubbing earth between his fingers and mixing wet mulch around the sapling's base. "It is not about planting one tree or two trees or 1,000 trees.

items.title: Trump's diplomatic week lays bare the limits of his power
items.summary: FROM his high-profile address at the United Nations General Assembly to his high-stakes White House summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, United States President Donald Trump this week was looking to reassert himself on the world stage. Trump has begun facing pushback from world leaders on issues ranging from the crisis in the Middle East to Russia's war in Ukraine, leaving the impression of a foreign policy agenda that has stalled. Iran's defiance has become the most intractable foreign policy challenge of Trump's second term.

items.title: NST Leader: Shared patterns of persecution make Rohingya and Gaza two sides of same coin
items.summary: Yet, similar persecution is occurring in Malaysia's regional backyard: Myanmar's annihilation and displacement of the Rohingya. This stateless Muslim minority populate Myanmar's Rakhine state, on the country's northwestern coast bordering Bangladesh. Rohingya and Palestinians share uncanny patterns of persecution and state-sanctioned aggression, contrasted only by historical and political circumstances.

items.title: Kamaruddin will 'continue exco duties unless instructed otherwise'
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Kelantan Bersatu chairman Datuk Kamaruddin Md Nor said he would leave any decision on his position as a state executive councillor to the state government amid a dispute between Bersatu and Perikatan Nasional (PN). The dispute resulted in the suspension of PN activities effective Wednesday. Kamaruddin, who is also the state executive councillor for tourism, culture, arts and heritage, said he would continue carrying out his duties as usual unless instructed otherwise by Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.

items.title: Cockroaches, rat droppings: Two popular Sungai Besar eateries ordered shut for 14 days
items.summary: SABAK BERNAM: Two popular food premises in Sungai Besar were ordered closed for 14 days after inspectors found various hygiene offences during Ops Bersih Premis Makanan yesterday. "Two premises were ordered closed for 14 days under the Food Establishment By-Laws (Sabak Bernam District Council) 2007. MDSB said it would continue conducting regular inspections and monitoring of food premises to ensure hygiene and food safety standards were complied with.

items.title: 'I have no information,' Tuan Ibrahim on BN talks
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Perikatan Nasional (PN) deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said he had no information on whether the coalition was among two political coalitions scheduled to meet Barisan Nasional (BN) next week to discuss possible cooperation ahead of the Melaka election. Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the coalition would hold separate meetings with two political coalitions next week to discuss possible cooperation in the Melaka election. The meetings will be led by Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, together with top leaders of the two coalitions.

items.title: Six dead after explosion destroys building in Athens
items.summary: ATHENS: Six people have died, the Greek fire brigade said on Saturday, after a two-storey residential building in a tourist area of central Athens collapsed following an explosion which the capital's mayor said was likely linked to gas infrastructure. Emergency crews in heavy gear and red helmets assisted by rescue dogs, cameras and sensors found the bodies of six people, fire brigade spokesman Vassilis Vathrakogiannis said in a televised briefing. The tourists, two American couples, had been expected to check in to catch a flight from Athens airport at 3pm local time on Friday but did not show up, a police source said.

items.title: Goh Sze Fei‑Nur Izzuddin storm into quarterfinals as Pearly Tan‑Thinaah sparkle with straight‑set wins
items.summary: NAGOYA, Sept 26 — Malaysia’s national professional men’s doubles pair, Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani, are one step away from securing a medal at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games after advancing to the quarterfinals following a straight-set victory over Japan’s Yugo Kobayashi-Takuro Hoki today. During the match held at the Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium, the national pair faced no major issues in claiming a 21-19, 21-16 straight-set win. Meanwhile, another national men’s doubles pair, Aaron Chia and Tee Kai Wun, fell short of reaching the quarterfinals of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after bowing out to South Korea’s world number one pair, Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, in straight sets of 21-19, 21-16.

items.title: As heavy rain and flooding continue in Bangkok, Malaysians urged to stay vigilant
items.summary: BANGKOK, Sept 26 — Malaysians in Bangkok have been urged to exercise caution and remain vigilant as persistent heavy rain and flooding continue to disrupt roads and daily activities across the Thai capital, with all 50 districts declared disaster zones. In an advisory issued Saturday, the Malaysian Embassy in Bangkok urged Malaysians residing in or travelling to the city to keep abreast of the latest weather, road, and traffic conditions and plan their journeys in advance. It said the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA) provides an online Road Flood Monitoring System that allows the public to check road conditions and water levels at monitoring points across the capital.

items.title: Fama readies warehouses nationwide with buffer stocks as El Niño threat rises
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Sept 26 — The Federal Agricultural Marketing Authority (Fama) has taken proactive steps to safeguard the nation’s food supply by establishing a special committee two months ago to prepare for the possible impact of El Nino. Its chairman, Abang Ahmad Kerdee Abang Masagus, said the move reflected Fama’s early action to prepare for the phenomenon, including plans to procure and store agro-food products at Fama warehouses nationwide. “At Fama, we established a committee two months ago.

items.title: Storm clouds gather: MetMalaysia issues urgent alert for Kuala Lumpur and 12 states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 8pm today. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Hilir Perak, Bagan Datuk, Muallim, Batang Padang, Perak Tengah, Kinta, Kampar and Manjung in Perak; Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Machang, Tanah Merah and Jeli in Kelantan. Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pulau Tioman, Temerloh, Jerantut and Kuantan in Pahang; Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling and Klang in Selangor; Kuala Pilah, Tampin, Rembau and Jempol in Negeri Sembilan; and Mersing in Johor.

items.title: Madani Mart’s master licensing push could fuel 300 outlets, says Fuziah
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 26 — Madani Mart is opening master licensing applications to companies, investors, and strategic partners with financial and operational capabilities to accelerate its retail network expansion nationwide. Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said each party appointed by Yayasan Madani will have the opportunity to develop and operate up to 100 Madani Mart branches, subject to set terms and standards. She said expansion through this model will begin after Yayasan Madani ensures the supply chain and pricing for about 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs) offered by Madani Mart remain stable.

items.title: Van impaled by guardrail in Kuching crash, passenger injured
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 26 — A passenger van was impaled by a roadside guardrail after crashing at a traffic light junction in Bandar Baru Samariang this morning. See Hua Daily News reported that the incident occurred at about 7am today. The van was carrying one female passenger at the time.

items.title: Anwar questions Opposition priorities: ‘No salary, they’re angry; those who steal, they don’t mention’
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today questioned the federal Opposition’s priorities, taking a swipe at its MPs for scrutinising his refusal to draw a prime ministerial salary while, he said, saying little about those who “ sakau ”, or steal, large sums of money. Anwar recalled being questioned by Opposition MPs in Parliament over how he could support himself without taking his salary as prime minister. Anwar said the government also provides the vehicle he uses, accommodation at the prime minister’s official residence, Seri Perdana, and flights.

items.title: PBS to reinforce unity and integrity while remaining in GRS, says president
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Parti Bersatu Sabah (PBS) president Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam wants the party to be strengthened as a modern, multiracial and integrity-driven entity that remains relevant, while reaffirming its commitment to continue working with Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS). He said the direction of the new PBS leadership would be based on three main pillars — unity, stability and integrity — in line with the theme of the 41st PBS Congress held today, ‘Unity, Stability, Integrity’. He said the struggle concerning the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) was not yet over and PBS would continue to play an active role in defending Sabah’s rights and interests.

items.title: Kuala Pilah Form Two student death: Cause still undetermined after post-mortem, police question 21
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — A post-mortem has failed to establish the cause of death of a 14-year-old boy whose death is being investigated following allegations of bullying at a school hostel in Kuala Pilah, with police awaiting the results of further tests. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the examination was carried out at the Forensic Medicine Department of Tuanku Jaafar Hospital in Seremban from 10.30am today, Harian Metro reported. He said police had so far recorded statements from 21 people, including students, teachers and the boy’s parents, as part of the investigation.

items.title: Govt to announce firm measures to ensure fair wages in Budget 2027, says Anwar
items.summary: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was currently at the final stage of preparing the budget and would formulate more concerted efforts to ensure that wage increases were commensurate with graduates’ qualifications. Take South Korea, for example, particularly where productivity is high, and wages have also increased accordingly. items.title: Anwar says he has not received Loke’s resignation letter
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has yet to receive Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s resignation letter. Loke offered to resign following a DAP Central Executive Committee (CEC) meeting on September 19 in response to the conditional pardon granted to former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. RoS issued the suspension order, effective September 23, covering all PN activities.

items.title: ‘Not a zero-sum game’: Anwar says he wants to help Malays, but not by denying others’ rights
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said he wants to help Malays in the country, while stressing that this should not come at the expense of the rights of others because it is not a “zero-sum game”. “But I ‘ tidak senang ’ (dislike) any views that insult others, that belittle others’ roles or deny the rights of others. Just before making the remarks, Anwar invited UiTM alumni to select seven to 10 representatives to evaluate programmes under Bumiputera agencies, including UiTM itself, and propose improvements.

items.title: Khaled Nordin: Malaysia to reinforce defence, especially in Sabah, amid South China Sea tensions
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — Malaysia needs to strengthen its national defence, particularly in Sabah, as a precaution in the event of a clash between major powers in the South China Sea. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia’s main concern was the possibility of a conflict or unexpected incident in the area that could have spillover effects on the country, particularly Sabah. “Every country has its own right to strengthen its national defence.

items.title: Woman loses RM1.15m after falling for love scam syndicate in Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 26 — A farmer and agricultural product trader lost more than RM1.15 million after falling victim to a love scam syndicate. Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 50-year-old woman, befriended an individual known as Siew Gui Lim @ Jason via WhatsApp on July 17 before their relationship grew closer. “The suspect then posed as a cybersecurity consulting director and offered a gold investment, promising the victim profits.

items.title: Anwar says company losses are not a crime — fraud, abuse and ‘sakau’ are another matter
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Companies should not be penalised simply because they make losses, but action should be taken where there is fraud, abuse of power or “ sakau ”, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Speaking after addressing issues including the scrutiny of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Anwar said companies could go through periods of losses as well as profits, and that losses alone should not be grounds for punishment. Turning to UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, Anwar cautioned against passing judgment before its position had been properly examined.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast across much of Malaysia until this evening
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas across the country, except Sarawak, until 5pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Yan, Kuala Muda, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they comprise Kerian, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kuala Kangsar, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Bagan Datuk and Hilir Perak. In Pahang, the areas involved are Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub and Bentong, while in Selangor, the warning covers Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor and Klang.

items.title: Mindef launches national defence literacy drive to prepare public for new security threats
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 26 — The Defence Ministry (Mindef) today launched the National Defence Literacy Programme to boost the public’s awareness, knowledge and understanding of national defence, security and sovereignty. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said a shifting security threat landscape demands a deeper understanding of national defence, and a recognition of the role Malaysians can play in safeguarding the nation’s sovereignty. “This is where what we call defence literacy comes in.

items.title: Anwar: UiTM Jalan Othman Campus renamed in honour of Arshad Ayub, architect of institution’s early growth
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that Universiti Teknologi MARA’s (UiTM) Jalan Othman Campus in Petaling Jaya has been renamed UiTM Tun Arshad Ayub Jalan Othman Campus in recognition of the late educationist’s contributions to the development of the institution. Anwar said the renaming was a tribute to Arshad’s legacy, having played a key role in the development of the Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM) into UiTM, while also being known for his firm emphasis on educational quality, good governance and expanding educational opportunities for Bumiputera students. Anwar said Arshad had also maintained a strong commitment to governance and institutional integrity, rather than using Malay institutions or agencies for personal gain or allowing them to be undermined by misconduct.

items.title: Akmal Nasrullah: Removing 30pc Bumiputera equity rule for private education will not weaken empowerment agenda
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Sept 26 — The removal of the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for private education institutions (IPS) will not undermine the government’s agenda to empower the community, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said today. At the event, the minister was also presented with the RIYI 2026 closing summary report, which highlighted a gap between students’ expectations and employers’ assessments of graduates’ workplace readiness. Meanwhile, 62 per cent of students said they felt adequately prepared by their universities, while only 32.3 per cent of employers agreed that local universities sufficiently prepared graduates for workplace realities.

items.title: Sarawak to set up authority to manage and develop lakes, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 26 — Sarawak will establish an authority to oversee, manage and develop the state’s lake areas in a comprehensive manner. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the initiative is part of the state’s development plans for the next five years. Meanwhile, he said the Centre for Technology Excellence Sarawak (CENTEXS) would establish a Flying School Academy in Betong to support the state’s efforts to advance modern agriculture through drone technology.

items.title: Kuskop channels nearly RM10b to 270,000 entrepreneurs as of August, seeks bigger Budget 2027 allocation, says minister
items.summary: BATU KAWAN, Sept 26 — The Ministry of Entrepreneur and Cooperatives Development (Kuskop) has channelled nearly RM10 billion through various support and financing programmes under the ‘Power Up 10K’ initiative to about 270,000 entrepreneurs nationwide as of the end of August. “The RM10 billion is part of the RM15 billion target to be channelled to the MSME and cooperative sectors this year. Sim noted that financing support for the MSME sector had been increased to RM60 billion this year from RM50 billion previously.
